Rashi on Eruvin 5a:10:1.hebrew: ואי אמרת בד' הוי מבוי היאך ניתר באורך ארבעה - מכדי, מיעוט חצירות שתים, ואין פתח פחות מד', ואיך יפתח פתח רוחבו ארבעה במשך המבוי, שאינו אלא ד', איה מקום הפצימין? ועוד כולו פרוץ הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 5a:10:1.english: And if you say the mabbui is four [cubits] wide, how can it be permitted with a length of four? - Since the minimum number of courtyards [on its sides] is two, and a doorway is not less than four [cubits] wide, how could one make a four-cubit doorway along the length of the mabbui, which is only four? Where is the room for the doorposts? Moreover, the whole [mabbui] is open.

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:11:1.hebrew: וכי תימא דפתח ליה בדופן אמצעית - וכי קאמר רב יוסף הכשר מבוי באורך ד' במבוי רחב מאד, קאמר ויכול לפתוח פתח החצירות בדופן שמאחריו:
Rashi on Eruvin 5a:11:1.english: And if you say that he made an opening for him in the middle wall - When Rav Yosef said that a mabui is rendered valid by a length of four cubits, he said it about a very wide mabui, and he can open the courtyard openings in the wall behind it.

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:11:2.english: But Rav Nachman said: "We hold" - A tradition from our forefathers, a custom from our teachers.

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:11:3.hebrew: ארכו יתר על רחבו - הוי מבוי וניתר בלחי וקורה, אבל מרובע דין חצר עליו, ואמרי' לקמן חצר צריכה פס ד' או פס משהו מכאן ופס משהו מכאן, היכא דפריצה במלואה לרה"ר, וכיון דאמרת ארכו ד' כשר, הרי רחבו ד' חסר משהו, ואין שם שיעור פתח, דבכולי הך מסכתא אמרי' דאין פתח פחות מד':
Rashi on Eruvin 5a:11:3.english: Its length exceeds its width - This means it is an alleyway closed off by a cheek-post and a beam. But if it is square, the law of a courtyard applies to it. As the Gemara says later, a courtyard requires a partition of four cubits, or of some lesser length, on this side and on that side, where the breach is entirely open to the public domain. Since you said its length is four cubits, it is valid. But then its width is four cubits less something, and there is no valid measure of an opening there, since throughout this entire tractate it is stated that an opening may not be less than four cubits.

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:12:1.english: In a corner - a handbreadth of the opening in the middle wall, and three handbreadths in the continuing wall, and likewise on its other side, as follows:

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:13:1.english: The cheek projecting from the wall of an alleyway - Into the width of the alleyway, and it is not made there for the sake of being a cheek. Rather, he extended his building at the side of his house, as people do for the sake of reinforcement:

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:1:1.english: And the one who says four holds that it is forbidden to use under the beam - Its inner edge descends and blocks, and the width of the beam lies outside the blockage. Those using the alley have no way to recognize the beam, since they are down low. Therefore the beam must extend into the alley, so that it is recognizable to them when they use it at that same height. And since one takes it out from under the beam, there must be a place that is recognizable and significant.

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:2:1.hebrew: לא דכולי עלמא מותר ובהא פליגי מר סבר קורה - שתיקנו חכמים למבוי משום היכר בעלמא הוא דלא ליתי למישרי רשות הרבים, והרי יש כאן היכר בכניסתן כשמשתמשין תחת הקורה:
Rashi on Eruvin 5a:2:1.english: No, everyone agrees it is permitted to use [the space] beneath a beam, and they disagree about this: one master holds [it is] a beam - The Sages instituted [the mavoy] merely as a marker, so that people would not come to permit the public domain. And indeed, there is a marker here at their entrance, when they use [the space] beneath the beam:

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:2:2.english: And the one who says four holds [that the] beam [permits] - [The beam] which permits in an alley; the reason is because of a partition, as we say that its outer edge descends and seals [the gap]. And the Sages said that when [the gap is] more than twenty [cubits], we do not say it descends and seals. Since there is no shortfall of four [tefachim], it is a partition made to be less than four [tefachim]. And it is established everywhere that a partition that is not fit for four [tefachim] is not a partition, since a private domain is not [formed] at less than four tefachim, even if it is enclosed by a partition of ten tefachim. And regarding the balconies of Chananya ben Akavya, too, we say that there are no partitions unless there are four [tefachim] within the space, in the chapter of Keitzad Mishtatfin (below, Eruvin 86b):

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:4:1.hebrew: גזירה שמא יפחת - על ידי דריסת רגלים יפחת המיעוט, ויעמוד על פחות מטפח, הלכך בעינן טפי, וכיון דאפיקתיה מהיכר של מעלה, אוקמיה אד' דחשיבי בכל דוכתא:
Rashi on Eruvin 5a:4:1.english: A decree, lest it diminish - By the trampling of feet, the minimum will diminish and fall below a tefach. Therefore we require more, and since we took it out from a marking above, we establish it as the 'four' that are significant in every place.

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:5:1.english: They drew it - Regarding carving into the length of the alleyway: where the carved part is a protrusion, such as a diminution, it is apt to speak of it as a "width" (rochav). Where the carved part is a recess surrounded by walls, such as a carving, it is apt to use the term "drawn" (mashach).

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:5:2.english: Rav Yosef - Who requires a tefach above, requires four here. In that case the beam already serves as a wall and comes to exclude, so a mere mark suffices. Here, however, it is only now that he makes it into a wall. For both Rav Yosef and Abaye, this wall must be visible for the full valid length of a complete mavoi. Therefore, for Rav Yosef the required length of the mavoi is four tefachim, while Abaye holds that it is four cubits:

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:6:1.english: That was breached on one of its sides - From the walls along its long side:

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:6:2.english: Toward its top - Close to the beam, from it and inward.

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:6:3.english: If there is a four-handbreadth ledge there - If a remnant of the wall was left standing, or one made a four-handbreadth ledge at the breach, adjacent to the beam:

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:6:4.hebrew: מתיר פירצה - אף על גב שנשתייר שם עדיין פירצה עד עשר, דכיון דיש הכשר אורך מבוי מן הקורה עד הפירצה, לא בטל ליה תורת פתח מקמאי, ובמלתיה קאי, וקורתו מתירתו, ופירצתה מתרת כיון דלאו יותר מעשר תורת פתח עליה, ומבוי אינו נפסל בפתחים הרבה. אי נמי, שבקו בני מבוי פתחא קמא ונפקו ועיילי בההיא פירצה משום דדרך קצרה היא להם, אפ"ה לא בטלה תורת פתח, וקורה מן הראשון, משום דהוי פתח לד' הסמוכין לו, הואיל וד' אורך ראויין לקורה, דיש בהן הכשר מבוי:
Rashi on Eruvin 5a:6:4.english: Permits a breach - Even though a breach of up to ten [handbreadths] remains there, since there is valid alley status for the length from the beam to the breach, the doorway status of the earlier [opening] is not nullified, and the matter stands on its own terms. Its beam permits the alley, and its breach permits it as well, since the breach is no more than ten [handbreadths] and it retains the status of a doorway. An alley is not disqualified by many doorways. Alternatively, the residents of the alley left the first doorway and went out and in through that breach, because it is a shorter route for them; even so, the doorway status is not nullified, and the beam from the first [doorway] still applies, because it counts as a doorway for the four cubits adjacent to it. Four cubits of length are fit for a beam, since they have the valid status of an alley.

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:7:1.english: And if not - because there is no *pas* (a wall section) of four [handbreadths].

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:7:2.english: Less than three - If the gap is less than three.

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:7:3.hebrew: מתיר - תיקון המבוי את המבוי, שהרי כלבוד דמי, ואין כאן פירצה, ואם הפירצה ג' אינו מתיר, דכיון דממעטין בני מבוי בהילוכן ומקצרין את דרכן דרך אותה פירצה, חיישינן דילמא שבקי פתחא רבה, ועיילי ונפקי בההיא פירצה, ובטיל ליה פתחא קמא, ובטלה קורה דידיה, ואין קורה למבוי זה, והאי טעמא מפרש לקמן בפירקין:
Rashi on Eruvin 5a:7:3.english: Permits - The repair of the alley [i.e., the beam] permits the alley itself, since it is considered as if it were enclosed (kilvud), and there is no gap here. But if the gap is three [handbreadths], it does not permit, because since the residents of the alley reduce their movements and shorten their path through that gap, we fear that they might abandon the large opening and enter and exit through that gap, and the first opening will be nullified, and its beam will be nullified, and this alley will have no beam. This reason is explained later in the chapter:

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:7:4.english: And Abaye does not hold [the view of] R. Ami and R. Asi - For [the Mishna] speaks of validating an alley with four cubits, and here too, if there is no four-cubit strip, this beam is not fit for that strip, and so there is no beam here:

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:8:1.hebrew: סוף מבוי - כגון הא דר' אמי ור' אסי שכבר היה מבוי ואירע בו פסול, ה"נ דלמיהדר לשוייה מבוי סגי בד' טפחים:
Rashi on Eruvin 5a:8:1.english: End of an alley - For example, the case of R. Ammi and R. Assi, where there was already an alley and a defect arose in it; here too, to restore it as an alley, four handbreadths suffice:

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:8:2.hebrew: תחילת מבוי - כגון גבי חקק, דהשתא קאתי לשוייה מבוי:
Rashi on Eruvin 5a:8:2.english: The beginning of an alley - Such as in the case of a notch [cut into a wall], since now he is coming to make it into an alley.

Rashi on Eruvin 5a:9:1.hebrew: בתים וחצרות - בתים פתוחין לחצירות וחצירות למבוי, שכן היה דרכן שאין בתים פתוחין אלא לחצריהן, וכל חצר האמור בהש"ס ובמשנה אינו אלא לפני הבית, אבל שאחורי הבית מוקצה או רחבה קרי ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 5a:9:1.english: Houses and courtyards - Houses open onto courtyards, and courtyards onto an alley. For it was their practice that houses did not open except into their own courtyards. Any courtyard mentioned in the Talmud and in the Mishnah refers only to the space in front of the house; the space behind the house is called a mukatzeh (a set-aside space) or a revachah (a broad space).

Tosafot on Eruvin 5a:10:1.hebrew: ואי בארבעה היכי משכחת לה - אע"ג דד' דקאמר רב יוסף, היינו דאיכא משהו טפי, דהמבוי אם אינו רוחב ד' אינו צריך לחי, כדרב אהילאי לקמן. ואי לא הוי טפי משהו, הוי ארכו כרחבו; מ"מ, באותו משהו אין מקום לפצימין לעמוד:
Tosafot on Eruvin 5a:10:1.english: And if [it is] in four, how can one find it? - Although Rav Yosef says 'four', this refers to a case where there is an extra bit (mashehu): for if the mavoi is not four cubits wide, it does not need a lechi (side-post), as Rav Ahilai states below. And if there were no extra bit, its length would equal its width; nevertheless, in that extra bit there is no room for the pitzimin to stand.

Tosafot on Eruvin 5a:13:1.hebrew: אמר אביי מנא אמינא לה - הא דלא מייתי ראייה מלקמן (עירובין ד' י.) דאמר שמואל משמיה דלוי, מבוי שרחבו כ' אמה עושה פס גבוה עשרה במשך ארבע אמות ומעמידו לארכו של מבוי, שמא לחלק מבוי לב' מבואות, מודה רב יוסף דצריך ד' אמות:
Tosafot on Eruvin 5a:13:1.english: Abaye said: How do I know this? - That [the Gemara] does not bring a proof from below (Eruvin 10a), where Shmuel says in the name of Levi: an alley whose width is twenty cubits makes a pas (partition) ten handbreadths high, for a length of four cubits, and places it along the length of the alley, lest one divide the alley into two alleys; Rav Yosef concedes that four cubits are required.

Tosafot on Eruvin 5a:14:1.hebrew: ורב יוסף לאפוקי מתורת לחי עד דאיכא ד' אמות - קשה, דרב יוסף גופיה קאמר לקמן (עירובין ד' י.) על דברי רב הונא משך מבוי ארבע אמות, ודוחק לומר דהיינו לאפוקי מתורת לחי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 5a:14:1.english: And Rav Yosef [says]: to exclude [the law of] lechi, until there are four cubits - This is difficult: Rav Yosef himself says later (Eruvin ד' י.) in response to Rav Huna's statement that the length of an alleyway is four cubits, and it is a stretch to say that this is meant to exclude [the law of] lechi.

Tosafot on Eruvin 5a:15:1.hebrew: לחי הבולט מדופנו של מבוי - אין פירושו כההיא דלקמן (עירובין ד' י.) לחי המושך מדופנו של מבוי, דהתם מושך חוץ למבוי לארכו של מבוי, דהא חשיב ליה שוה מבפנים; והכא בולט לרחבו של מבוי וסותמו, דאמר לקמן דמבוי ז' ניתר בעומד מרובה על הפרוץ, ואביי הוה מצי לאתויי נמי מהתם:
Tosafot on Eruvin 5a:15:1.english: A lechi protruding from the side of an alley - This does not mean like the one taught below, a lechi extending from the side of an alley. For there it extends outside the alley lengthwise, since it is considered even [in width] on the inside; whereas here it protrudes across the width of the alley and closes it off. For it is stated below that an alley of seven [amot] is permitted when the standing [barrier] exceeds the open [space]; and Abaye could have cited [his proof] from there as well:

Tosafot on Eruvin 5a:8:1.hebrew: סוף מבוי הכי נמי - פירוש, כיון שלא נפסלה שנשתייר שם פס ד' דמבוי, כשר; אינו יוצא מתורת הכשר עד שיפחות שלא ישאר שם ד'. אבל תחלת מבוי, דהיינו שלא נשתייר שם פס ד', שצריך לעשות לו הכשר, צריך ד' אמות. וכן משמע לישנא דקאמר 'אם יש שם פס ד'', מכלל דבנשתייר שם פס ד' מיירי. ופרש"י אין נראה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 5a:8:1.english: The end of an alleyway, so too - Explanation: since it was not invalidated, in that a four-handbreadth wall-strip (pas) of the alleyway remained standing there, the alleyway is valid. It does not lose the status of validity until it is reduced so that no four handbreadths remain there. But the beginning of an alleyway, that is, where no four-handbreadth strip remained and which therefore requires a valid enclosure to be made for it, requires four cubits. So too the wording of the Gemara indicates, when it says 'if there is a four-handbreadth strip there': this implies that it is speaking of a case where a four-handbreadth strip remained. Rashi's explanation does not seem correct.
